canonical_statement: REPLENISH evaluated the efficacy and safety of secukinumab 300 mg and 150 mg, each combined with a 24-week prednisone taper, versus placebo plus the same taper in patients with recently relapsed polymyalgia rheumatica.
REPLENISH was a phase 3, double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled trial conducted at 148 sites in 28 countries.
The sponsor, Novartis, and the steering committee were involved in trial design; investigators collected data, and the sponsor performed site monitoring, data collation, and analysis.

Eligible patients were at least 50 years old, met EULAR-ACR polymyalgia rheumatica classification criteria, had bilateral shoulder pain, and had elevated C-reactive protein (at least 10 mg/L) or erythrocyte sedimentation rate (at least 30 mm/hr).
Patients had to have at least one polymyalgia rheumatica relapse while tapering prednisone or equivalent at a dose of at least 5 mg/day within 12 weeks before baseline.

population.label: Recently relapsed polymyalgia rheumatica
inclusion_criteria: At least one relapse during glucocorticoid taper at >=5 mg/day within 12 weeks before baseline

canonical_statement: Patients had to have received prednisone or equivalent at a dose of at least 10 mg/day for at least 8 consecutive weeks before screening.

population.label: Recently relapsed polymyalgia rheumatica
inclusion_criteria: Prior prednisone-equivalent exposure >=10 mg/day for >=8 consecutive weeks

canonical_statement: Patients with a history or evidence of giant-cell arteritis, rheumatoid arthritis, or other inflammatory arthritis were excluded.
The SEC-300 group received secukinumab 300 mg subcutaneously weekly through week 4 and every 4 weeks thereafter for 52 weeks.

canonical_statement: All three treatment groups received the same protocol-specified prednisone taper beginning at either 10 mg/day or 15 mg/day and intended to finish over 24 weeks.

canonical_statement: Randomization was stratified by Japan versus non-Japan; in the non-Japan population it was further stratified by baseline prednisone dose of 10 mg/day versus 15 mg/day.
Before week 12, the prednisone taper permitted limited protocol-defined adjustments, but subsequent alterations to the taper were not allowed.
Escape treatment consisted of increasing or restarting glucocorticoids while continuing the assigned blinded secukinumab or placebo regimen.
Rescue treatment consisted of alternative therapy chosen by the investigator; patients receiving rescue treatment discontinued secukinumab or placebo.
Remission was defined as absence of signs or symptoms attributable to polymyalgia rheumatica and no new diagnosis of giant-cell arteritis that warranted escape or rescue treatment.

outcome.definition: No PMR-attributable signs or symptoms and no new GCA diagnosis warranting escape or rescue treatment

canonical_statement: The primary outcome, sustained remission at week 52, required remission by week 12 that remained sustained through week 52 without PMR recurrence or a new giant-cell arteritis diagnosis warranting treatment.

outcome.definition: Remission by week 12 sustained to week 52 without PMR recurrence or new GCA requiring treatment

canonical_statement: Complete sustained remission at week 52 required sustained remission plus no qualifying elevation of inflammatory markers at two or more consecutive visits from week 12 through week 52.

outcome.definition: Sustained remission plus no qualifying ESR or high-sensitivity CRP elevation at >=2 consecutive visits from weeks 12-52

canonical_statement: A secondary outcome was the adjusted annual cumulative glucocorticoid dose through week 52, incorporating protocol taper, escape/rescue glucocorticoids, and other glucocorticoids converted to prednisone equivalents.

outcome.definition: Annualized total glucocorticoid exposure in prednisone equivalents through discontinuation or week 52

canonical_statement: A secondary outcome was time to first use of escape or rescue treatment through week 52.

concept.text: Time to first escape or rescue treatment

canonical_statement: FACIT-Fatigue was a secondary patient-reported outcome; scores range from 0 to 52, with higher scores indicating less fatigue.

outcome.definition: 0-52 scale; higher scores indicate less fatigue

canonical_statement: HAQ-DI was a secondary patient-reported outcome; scores range from 0 to 3, with higher scores indicating worse functioning.

outcome.definition: 0-3 scale; higher scores indicate worse functioning

canonical_statement: Glucocorticoid-related toxic effects at week 52 were exploratory outcomes measured with the GTI Aggregate Improvement Score and Cumulative Worsening Score, excluding the bone mineral density domain.

outcome.definition: GTI-AIS and GTI-CWS excluding bone mineral density domain

canonical_statement: The planned enrollment of at least 120 patients per group provided 90% power at a two-sided 5% type I error rate assuming sustained remission in 50% of secukinumab-treated patients and 29% of placebo-treated patients.
A sequential testing strategy was used across primary and secondary outcomes to maintain a family-wise type I error rate of 5%.
For the primary estimand, trial-regimen discontinuation or prohibited medication use before week 52 were handled with a composite strategy and classified as nonresponse.
The primary analysis used logistic regression adjusted for baseline prednisone dose, region, and sex.
Sensitivity analyses included a tipping-point analysis, and a supplementary estimand used a treatment-policy strategy for treatment discontinuation and prohibited medication use.
Safety was assessed in all patients who received at least one dose of secukinumab or placebo and was summarized descriptively for treatment-emergent adverse events.
Of 474 patients screened from March 2023 through July 2024, 381 underwent randomization, with 127 assigned to each group.

canonical_statement: The Supplementary Appendix specified that before week 12, either up to two prednisone taper intervals could be prolonged to 4 weeks or the prednisone dose could be increased once by one taper step; these adjustment options were mutually exclusive.

The Supplementary Appendix specified nonresponder imputation for primary-endpoint data missing at week 52, except that intermittent missing PMR assessments could be imputed as remission when remission was present both before and after the missing visit.

canonical_statement: The authors concluded that secukinumab 300 mg or 150 mg combined with a 24-week glucocorticoid taper produced superior sustained-remission efficacy at week 52 compared with the glucocorticoid taper alone.
The authors concluded that secukinumab treatment had a glucocorticoid-sparing effect in patients with recently relapsed polymyalgia rheumatica.

The authors interpreted the overall safety findings as aligned with the known safety profile of secukinumab in approved indications, while noting that infections and hypersensitivity reactions were more common with secukinumab.
The trial did not provide efficacy data beyond 1 year.

The placebo group had a higher rate of trial-regimen discontinuation than the secukinumab groups, which the authors noted might have led to underdetection of adverse events associated with conventional treatment.
It remained uncertain whether remission in the placebo group would have been higher if glucocorticoids had been administered for 52 weeks instead of the protocol 24-week taper.
The REPLENISH trial was funded by Novartis.
Author disclosure forms were provided with the full text of the article at NEJM.org.
A data-sharing statement was provided with the full text of the article at NEJM.org.
